stories.headline: Iran strikes commercial ships in Hormuz; tankers hit near Iraq as war spreads to Gulf shipping

key_facts.fact: Three commercial ships were struck by projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz on March 11, including the Thai-flagged bulk carrier Mayuree Naree (hit 11 nautical miles north of Oman), which caught fire and forced crew evacuation with 3 mariners reported missing.
key_facts.excerpt: The conflict in the Strait of Hormuz intensified on Wednesday as the Iranian navy confirmed it targeted at least two of three ships struck by projectiles in the critical passage for the oil and shipping trades.

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC confirmed targeting the Express Room (Liberian-flagged) and Mayuree Naree, claiming both vessels 'ignored alerts and warnings from the IRGC Navy.' IRGC Commander Adm. Alireza Tangsiri declared: 'Every vessel intending to pass must obtain permission from Iran.'
key_facts.excerpt: IRGC Commander Adm. Alireza Tangsiri declared: 'Every vessel intending to pass must obtain permission from Iran.' An IRGC spokesperson asserted the Strait was 'under the intelligent management of the brave naval forces.'

key_facts.fact: A Japanese container vessel owned by Mitsui was among the ships hit. Kpler analyst Dimitris Ampatzidis warned: 'This increasingly points to a sustained pattern rather than isolated incidents. The pace of attacks does not suggest any intention to de-escalate.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'This increasingly points to a sustained pattern rather than isolated incidents,' said Dimitris Ampatzidis, a senior risk and compliance analyst at Kpler. 'The pace of attacks does not suggest any intention to de-escalate.'

key_facts.fact: On March 12, two fuel tankers were attacked near the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr by what appeared to be Iranian boats rigged with explosives, killing one person with 38 rescued. Iraqi oil ports stopped operations following the attack.
key_facts.excerpt: One person was killed and another 38 people were rescued after the incident near the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr, which Reuters and CNN reported appeared to be caused by Iranian boats rigged with explosives.

key_facts.fact: The attacks bring the total vessels struck since the start of the war on Feb 28 to at least 16, with the Strait of Hormuz carrying about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption.
key_facts.excerpt: The strait carries about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption and serves as the primary export route for Gulf oil producers.

stories.headline: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 2817 condemning Iran's attacks on Gulf states, 13-0-2

key_facts.fact: The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2817 on March 11 condemning Iran's 'egregious attacks' against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Jordan, with 13 votes in favor, none against, and China and Russia abstaining.
key_facts.excerpt: The 15-member Council adopted resolution 2817 (2026) by a vote of 13 in favour to none against, with 2 abstentions (China, Russian Federation).

key_facts.fact: The Bahrain-led resolution was cosponsored by approximately 135 UN member states, described as the largest number of countries ever to cosponsor a Security Council draft resolution.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We believe that this is the largest number of countries ever to cosponsor a Security Council draft resolution,' he said.

key_facts.fact: The resolution demands immediate cessation of Iranian attacks, halt to threats and provocations, cessation of interference with maritime trade, and discontinuation of support to proxy groups. Iran called it 'a manifest injustice against my country.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran called the resolution 'a manifest injustice against my country.'

key_facts.fact: A second draft resolution tabled by the Russian Federation, described by Moscow as an 'impartial document' that intentionally avoided naming specific parties, was rejected with only 4 votes in favor, 2 against, and 9 abstentions.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow presented a second resolution it described as an 'impartial document' that intentionally avoided naming specific parties. This draft was rejected 4-2 with 9 abstentions.

stories.headline: Oil surges above $100 as Iran vows to keep Hormuz shut; IEA calls it largest supply disruption ever

key_facts.fact: Brent crude surged more than 9% to briefly cross $100/barrel (touching $101.59) on March 12, while WTI rose nearly 9% above $95, after Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed as a 'tool of pressure.'
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude oil hovered around $100 a barrel Thursday, after Iran's new leader purportedly said the Strait of Hormuz would remain shut... Mojtaba Khamenei warned that the strait would remain closed as a 'tool of pressure.'

key_facts.fact: The IEA said the war in Iran is 'creating the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market,' noting that 7.5% of global supply has now been disrupted. This came just 24 hours after the IEA announced a record 400 million barrel reserve release.
key_facts.excerpt: The war in Iran is now 'creating the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market,' the IEA said in a report on Thursday, noting that 7.5% of global supply has now been disrupted.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, the Dow dropped 553 points (1.2%), and the Nasdaq fell 1.4%. US crude oil prices have risen more than 40% since the start of the war, with retail gas prices up nearly 70 cents to $3.59/gallon.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. crude oil prices have now risen more than 40% since the start of the war, bringing retail gas prices along with them. Since March 1, gas prices have risen nearly 70 cents to $3.59 per gallon.

key_facts.fact: The price spike occurred despite the historic 400 million barrel reserve release by G7 nations announced the previous day, underscoring the severity of the disruption as tanker traffic through Hormuz has 'all but stopped.'
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices climbed back above $100 per barrel Thursday after attacks on commercial shipping in the Persian Gulf raised fears of further disruptions to global energy supplies, despite a record release of emergency reserves by major consuming nations.

stories.headline: Russia giving Iran specific drone tactics from Ukraine war to hit US and Gulf targets, intel says

key_facts.fact: Russia is helping Iran with advanced drone tactics drawn from its war in Ukraine to hit US and Gulf nation targets in the Middle East, according to a Western intelligence official cited by CNN on March 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia is helping Iran with advanced drone tactics from its war in Ukraine to hit US and Gulf nation targets in the Middle East, according to a Western intelligence official.

key_facts.fact: Shahed drones, designed by Iran but mass-produced by Moscow for use in Ukraine, have been unexpectedly successful in penetrating air defenses in the Gulf conflict. Russia is sharing specific tactical advice that marks a new level of Kremlin support for Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Shahed drones, designed by Iran but mass-produced by Moscow for use in Ukraine, have been unexpectedly successful in penetrating the air defenses.

key_facts.fact: The intelligence revelation coincides with Russia abstaining rather than vetoing the UN Security Council resolution condemning Iran's attacks on Gulf states, suggesting a nuanced Kremlin approach of providing covert military support while avoiding overt diplomatic confrontation.
key_facts.excerpt: The specific tactical advice marks a new level of support from the Kremlin.

stories.headline: Ukraine records first net territorial gains since 2023, reclaims 400+ sq km in counterattacks

key_facts.fact: For the first time since the summer 2023 counteroffensive, Ukrainian forces liberated more territory than they lost during the final weeks of February 2026, according to ISW data published March 11. Ukrainian forces have reclaimed approximately 257 square kilometers since January 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time in almost three years, Kyiv began regaining some territory.

key_facts.fact: ISW data shows net gains of nearly 33 square kilometers between February 14-20, followed by approximately 57 square kilometers from February 21-27. The last comparable gains were during the Summer 2023 counteroffensive.
key_facts.excerpt: Between February 14 and 20, Ukrainian troops achieved a net gain of nearly 33 square kilometers, while from February 21 to 27 they recorded a net gain of approximately 57 square kilometers.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Gen. Staff official Oleksandr Komarenko said Ukrainian airborne assault troops and mechanized brigades have liberated more than 400 square kilometers, nearly restoring full control of Dnipropetrovsk region with only a handful of small settlements remaining.
key_facts.excerpt: Oleksandr Komarenko, head of the main operational directorate of the general staff of Ukraine's armed forces, told local media that Ukrainian airborne assault troops and mechanized brigades had already liberated more than 400 square kilometers of territory.

key_facts.fact: The gains undermine Russia's buffer zone strategy along parts of the border and could disrupt Russian plans for a spring-summer offensive.
key_facts.excerpt: Pushing Russian forces back undermines Moscow's attempts to establish buffer zones along parts of the border, and could disrupt Russian plans for fresh attacks in the spring and summer.

stories.headline: Kremlin signals expanded demands on Ukraine, says 2022 Istanbul proposals 'no longer correspond to reality'

key_facts.fact: Kremlin Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated on March 11 that Russia's 2022 Istanbul ceasefire proposals are outdated, saying 'the whole reality has changed.' Russian state media framed Peskov's statement as saying the proposals no longer 'correspond to the changed situation.'
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov responded to a question on March 11 about whether Russia remains committed to the 2022 Istanbul proposals, stating that 'the whole reality has changed.'

key_facts.fact: Russian Federation Council International Affairs Committee Chairperson Grigory Karasin called the 2022 Istanbul proposals and the 'caravan of international relations' now 'irrelevant' as four years have passed, calling on Ukraine to 'end this adventure' — meaning capitulation.
key_facts.excerpt: Karasin claimed that the 2022 Istanbul proposals and the 'caravan of international relations' are now 'irrelevant' as four years have passed and Ukraine's leadership was and remains 'unwilling to negotiate.'

key_facts.fact: ISW assessed the Kremlin is 'likely setting informational conditions to expand Russian demands of Ukraine and NATO by making it clear that its current demands are no longer sufficient,' with multiple Russian officials and state media amplifying the messaging.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin is likely setting informational conditions to expand Russian demands of Ukraine and NATO by making it clear that its current demands are no longer sufficient.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Zelenskyy told POLITICO on March 11 that Ukraine needs 'more pressure on Russia, not on me,' urging Trump to stop pushing Ukraine toward Russia's terms. Zelenskyy said Ukrainians are 'tired' but not ready to accept Russia's ultimatums.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We need negotiations. We support them,' Zelenskyy said. 'We don't trust Russia, but I think, and I trust that Americans really want to finish with this war. I hope that they will help us, but we need more pressure on Russia, not on me.'

stories.headline: Trump launches Section 301 trade probes into 16 economies to rebuild tariff regime after Supreme Court loss

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration on March 11 announced new trade investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into 16 economies: China, the EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan, and India.
key_facts.excerpt: Those being investigated are China, the EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan and India.

key_facts.fact: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the probes will focus on 'excess capacity and production' leading to persistent trade surpluses with the United States, as the administration works to rebuild its tariff authority after the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA-based reciprocal tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: The probes will focus on 'excess capacity and production' of foreign nations which Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said was leading to persistent trade surpluses with the United States.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted that by August, US tariffs would return to the levels that existed before the Supreme Court's ruling that struck down the IEEPA-based tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently predicted that by August, U.S. tariffs would return to the levels that existed before the Supreme Court's ruling.

key_facts.fact: The announcement came just weeks before a planned Beijing summit between Trump and Xi Jinping, raising the stakes on US-China trade relations. The probes are expected to be expanded to additional nations.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump raises the stakes on China with Section 301 trade probe, weeks before Beijing summit.

stories.headline: Immorta Bio reports combination senolytic-stem cell therapy achieved 84% lifespan extension in mice

key_facts.fact: Immorta Bio announced on March 11 that its combination of SenoVax (first-in-class senolytic immunotherapy) and StemCellRevivify (personalized mesenchymal stem cell platform) achieved approximately 73% increase in mean survival and 84% extension of median lifespan in validated murine aging models.
key_facts.excerpt: Immorta Bio Inc. today announced breakthrough preclinical results demonstrating dramatic lifespan extension in validated murine aging models using a novel dual-platform therapeutic strategy.

key_facts.fact: The combination therapy significantly outperformed either monotherapy, reducing senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) inflammatory markers and boosting regenerative biomarkers including Klotho, FGF-2, and GDF-11, with improved liver function and enhanced physical performance.
key_facts.excerpt: Combining Immorta Bio's vaccine and stem cell therapy doubled lifespan in a mouse model of aging... The combination also reduced markers of the SASP—inflammatory markers.

key_facts.fact: The research has been accepted for presentation at IMMUNOLOGY2026, the annual meeting of the American Association of Immunologists, to be held April 15-19 in Boston. CSO Dr. Thomas Ichim said the approach aims to 'address both the damage caused by aging and the decline in the body's ability to repair itself.'
key_facts.excerpt: Dr. Thomas Ichim: 'By combining immune-mediated clearance of senescent cells with regenerative cell therapy, we aim to address both the damage caused by aging and the decline in the body's ability to repair itself.'

key_facts.fact: The company is rapidly advancing toward IND-enabling studies, with initial clinical focus on liver disease and cancer. Studies used doxorubicin-induced systemic senescence and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver injury mouse models.
key_facts.excerpt: Rapidly advancing toward IND-enabling studies. Initial clinical focus on liver disease and cancer.
